name: vhs-filter
title: VHS Filter
description: A scene as recovered tape footage: colour smeared sideways off the brightness, the lines wobbling, a head-switch tear along the bottom edge, scanlines and grain. Runs its WebGL shader over its own built-in scene (a stat and a bar chart; label, number and bars from variables), not over the host video.
useWhen: A scene should read as recovered tape footage rather than a clean render: retro product spots, 'what we shipped in 2003' beats, lo-fi title cards.
You want the whole scene degraded for its full duration, not a one-frame artifact at a cut.
avoidWhen: The artifact should live only at the cut between two scenes: use glitch-cut.
Only a headline should break up: use rgb-glitch-text.
The story is the display or the glass rather than the signal: use crt-screen or camera-lens.
You want intermittent digital faults rather than continuous analog wear: use sustained-glitch.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Label
variables.description: Small caption above the number in the sample scene.

variables.label: Value
variables.description: The big number in the sample scene.

variables.label: Bars
variables.description: Bar heights as percentages, separated by commas (up to 12); the last bar is highlighted.

variables.label: Intensity
variables.description: 0 shows the scene, 1 the full tape look.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. The scanlines and grain are fine; lower renders faster but softens them.
